page.title: Best Foaming TPU Filament: Soft vs Firm, Hardness and Price per kg
page.desc: Foaming TPU compared by hardness range, spool size and price per kg: Siraya Tech TPU Air for soft parts, eSUN TPU-LW for firm, light parts at the lowest per-kg price, and colorFabb varioShore.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best foaming TPU filament for soft parts is Siraya Tech Flex TPU Air 85A: it foams down to 65A on a full 1 kg spool, from $42.99 (seen 2026-11-14). For firm, lightweight parts, the pick is the eSUN TPU-LW ({buy:esun-tpu-lw}): it runs from 93A down to 77A, at $38.65 per kg, the lowest per-kg price we found. The top complaint with every foaming TPU is stringing, because the filament keeps expanding in a hot nozzle and retraction stops working. Turn retraction off, print one part at a time, and dry the spool first (eSUN says 131 °F / 55 °C for 4 hours or more).

Foaming TPU carries a blowing agent. Print it hotter and it expands, so parts come out lighter and softer. Print it cooler and it stays dense and firm. You set the hardness with nozzle temperature and flow rate, so one spool covers a range. CNC Kitchen measured colorFabb varioShore at 92A when printed at 374 °F (190 °C) and 65A at 428 °F (220 °C), with the extrusion multiplier dropping from 113% to 57%. The other hardness figures in the table are the makers' own.
page.after:
What owners complain about

Stringing and oozing came up in 8 of the sources we read. Foaming filament keeps expanding in a hot nozzle, so retraction does little. eSUN and QIDI both say to turn it off and print one part at a time. CNC Kitchen called oozing on travel moves unavoidable and said to design parts around it.

Tuning came up 4 times. Each hardness needs its own temperature and flow pair. One Bambu Lab forum owner spent about two days tuning varioShore, and an eSUN TPU-LW owner said no online profile printed well. Print a small test cube at two or three temperatures before a big part.

Moisture came up 5 times. Wet TPU strings no matter how you tune it. Dry the spool before printing and print from a dry box.

Feeding came up 3 times. Soft filament can buckle in the extruder or jam an automatic feeder. eSUN says not to run TPU-LW through the Bambu Lab AMS.

Which one by need

Soft insoles, grips and parts that touch skin: Siraya Tech Flex TPU Air 85A. It reaches 65A on a full 1 kg spool from a US warehouse at $42.99.

Light parts that must keep their shape, such as cosplay armor, RC plane and drone bumpers, and covers: eSUN TPU-LW ({buy:esun-tpu-lw}). Its 93A firm end is stiffer than the others, and it costs the least per kg.

Settings you can trust out of the box: colorFabb varioShore TPU 95A. It has the most independent test data, and CNC Kitchen printed it on a Bowden Ender-3. It costs about twice as much per kg.

Not recommended

Foaming TPU is the wrong pick for parts that need exact dimensions or clean surfaces, such as press-fit gaskets. Use a regular 95A TPU for those. Skip QIDI TPU-Aero if you need it soon: it ships from China, and the page does not state the net spool weight.

notes:
HOW THE QUERY WAS CHOSEN: I tested five eSUN angles and dropped four. (1) LW-PLA for RC planes: Bambu PLA Aero was $26.99/1 kg on Bambu's US store on 2026-11-14 (sale; usual price $44.99), below eSUN PLA-LW at $28.99, and colorFabb LW-PLA foams lighter. eSUN wins no segment, so PLA-LW is a product record only. (2) 3 kg/5 kg PLA spools: SUNLU PLA+ 5 kg listed at $54.99 against eSUN's $68.99 (SUNLU price from search, not verified). (3) Bulk PETG: Kingroon, Anycubic and Elegoo reported at $8-10/kg against eSUN's $9.99/kg, so no clear win. (4) ESD filament: eSUN PETG-ESD and ABS-ESD showed 0 in stock in the US. (5) Foaming TPU: chosen. Few pages answer it beyond store listings and forum threads, and eSUN TPU-LW honestly wins on firmness (93A top end) and price per kg.

PAIN POINTS (counted across the sources I read): stringing/oozing because retraction fails with foaming material, 8 (CNC Kitchen; 2 Bambu forum threads with 3 users; eSUN spec page; QIDI page; Polyfab listing; Siraya blog snippet; colorFabb guide); tuning temperature and flow per hardness, 4; moisture and drying, 5; feeding/AMS/buckling, 3; price, 2 (eSUN cheaper than colorFabb, from the forum).

SEGMENTS AND WINNERS: soft parts at 65-70A (insoles, grips): Siraya Tech Flex TPU Air 85A, from $42.99 per 1 kg, US warehouse, 103 in stock. It is not an approved program, so it is named without a link. Firm lightweight parts and lowest per-kg price: eSUN TPU-LW, $28.99 per 0.75 kg = $38.65/kg, 93A to 77A. Proven settings and independent data: colorFabb varioShore 95A, $59.70 per 0.7 kg = $85.29/kg, measured 92A to 65A by CNC Kitchen.
